question: Rank worlds by adding up how good every life is. How good must lives be in a world 100 times as crowded to tie?
answer: Barely worth living, if only the total counts. Derek Parfit showed each step looks harmless: adding lives worth living harms no one, and sharing more evenly seems no loss. Follow the steps and an enormous, drab world outranks a happy one. He called it the repugnant conclusion; forty years on, nobody has an agreed way out.
move: Every reasonable-looking rule about population leads somewhere nobody accepts.
ask: Which of my goals keeps saying 'more is better', and would I stand by that if I followed it to the end?
source: Parfit, Reasons and Persons, 1984; the repugnant conclusion
reference: Parfit, Reasons and Persons, Oxford University Press, 1984, part four

scene.readout: Each life's score to tie, of 100

notes.text: A world of happy people. Score every life 100.
Twice the people at half the quality: the same total, so just as good.
Ten times the people at 10 each. Any better than 10 and the crowd wins.
A hundred times the people, lives barely worth living: the sum calls it a tie.
